answer: Each identity extends a Wesolowski VDF chain with one 20-minute proof per step, and publishes every output into a shared hash thread. Verifiers sample five random steps weekly and check them in under 50 milliseconds. A gap beyond 6 hours freezes the identity and forfeits its 15 token deposit. Squaring cannot be parallelized inside a chain, so 10,000 fakes need 10,000 dedicated cores, about $67,200 per 168-hour week at $0.04 per core-hour, plus 150,000 tokens lost to any outage. Keeping that swarm in lockstep every hour is like holding 10,000 marble clocks steady in a gale.
